writeup.headline: ConocoPhillips rates Buy on strong revenue growth and price momentum, with half its factors unscored.
writeup.thesis: COP's Buy rating and score of 76 rest on only three factors: growth, trend and news risk. Quality, balance sheet and valuation lacked enough data to score. Growth scores 85, driven by latest-quarter revenue growth of 43.3% year on year and TTM revenue growth of 9.2%, with growth sped up by 50.1 pp from the previous quarter. Trend scores 91: the price is 23.4% above its 200-day average, shares are up 45.9% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and the price is 1.5% below its 52-week high. News risk is neutral at 50, with no guidance change, no rating changes and no new litigation in the window. On valuation, P/S of 3.2x is moderate in absolute terms, but it is expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 50 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: Revenue swings with oil and gas prices, so the sharp quarterly growth may not last.
The shares have run up strongly and sit near their 52-week high, so a pullback is possible.
P/S is more expensive than at 50 of the last 61 month-ends.
Cash to debt of 0.33 means cash covers only about a third of debt.
The proposed Norway and Teesside sale and the 20-year LNG purchase deal carry execution and pricing uncertainty.
what_would_change: A gain of 4 points, for example from stronger growth or a positive news shift around Q3 results on Nov 5, would lift the rating to Strong Buy.
A drop of 12 points would push the rating to Hold, for example if growth fades or the price trend reverses sharply.
Scores for quality, balance sheet and valuation, once data is available, could move the composite either way, given the expensive reading against its own history.
